text.title: Fight over fossil fuels leaves COP31 climate talks in deadlock
text.body_text: - Published Negotiations at the COP31 UN climate summit in Turkey are in deadlock, having run through the night, as countries remain unable to agree on a new global climate deal.…
text.summary: Countries from nearly 200 countries are in a deadlock to try and get a new global climate agreement.

text.summary: The actor’s new role as James Bond could be bad news for DC, as a new owner, new chief and new director already threaten to shake and stir Gotham’s distinctive hero Can one actor play both Batman and James Bond? This is the question many have been asking since Robert Pattinson was announced as the new 007 . The obvious answer is yes: the 40-year-old Englishman has the poise, charisma and steel to join His Majesty’s Secret Service, and saving Gotham could soon become something he fits in between assignments. Among all the furore over Pattinson’s appointment, it would have been easy to miss some rather less cheering news for the citizens of Gotham. According to the Wrap , delays to The Batman: Part II have freed the actor from his contractual obligation to make a third film. The sequel is now due in February 2028, almost six years after the first instalment. He could still sign a new deal, of course, but Warner Bros will have to persuade its caped crusader to stick around. Continue reading...
